Portfolio Spotlight: Hex Security (YC W26) Most companies still rely on periodic penetration testing. But software now ships continuously, and the gap between audits is often where vulnerabilities emerge. In mid-September 2025, Anthropic detected a Chinese state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign that used AI to automate 80 to 90% of attack activity, with the system making thousands of requests, often multiple per second. Hex Security builds AI agents that run continuous penetration testing across applications, APIs and infrastructure. Instead of relying solely on annual testing, Hex’s agents operate 24/7 to find vulnerabilities, chain exploits and deliver verified findings with reproduction steps. The company is founded by Ahmad Khan , who previously worked on robotics and World Models; Huzaifa Ahmad , who previously built software at PlayAI, AWS and Capital One; and Prama Yudhistira , who previously worked on coding agents at Codegen and GPU firmware testing infrastructure at AMD. Input the tumor. Output the vaccine. Gamgee Technologies is building software that turns a dog’s tumor and healthy DNA into a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine design. Founder Paul Steven Conyngham spent 17 years in machine learning and had no biology background. When his dog Rosie was dying of cancer, he taught himself genomics, designed a vaccine around her tumor mutations, and coordinated the entire path from sequencing through manufacture and administration. Several of Rosie’s tumors shrank by 50-75%. Doing it by hand took a year and cost around $20,000. Gamgee’s target is a vaccine design in 48 hours at an end-to-end cost of $2,000. More than 300 dogs are already on the waitlist, and the company is preparing a clinician-led trial in 30 dogs to evaluate safety, immune response, and clinical outcomes. https://www.gamgee.io Congrats on the launch, Paul! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gbmFc2Kj

Our customers are the reason any of this is worth doing. They’re building what powers our everyday life, from data centers to offices to roads. None of this is possible without the hours, the late dinners, the high-fives, that extra push... it really takes a special team to create something special. I'm grateful I get to work with them every day.

We just made a customer's robots 30% faster AND 7% more successful. We never touched their hardware. Two most important KPIs for these robots in prod: faster and fewer failures. We used RL to improve both, which was not possible for them prior to working with us. This is because RL needs thousands of rollouts and feedback on which behaviors are better, and on a physical robot that means days of ops time. So we did all of it inside our world model simulator. Their policy runs closed-loop in our sim exactly as it does on hardware, which means we can roll out and evaluate candidate behaviors at massive scale, in parallel, with zero robot time. Inside that sim, we trained a small RL model that makes their policy faster and more reliable: trimming the wasted motion and editing out the failure modes. To prove this actually worked, they deployed our RL model on their real robots and evaluated the two head to head (base policy vs. base + RL): interleaved A/B on matched scenes, 2,000 episodes over a week, every episode human-rated. With our RL model on top, the robots delivered 30% more successful completions per robot-hour (p < 0.001), and task success rate improved 7% in absolute terms (p = 0.0008)! The improvement we measured in sim is the improvement they measured on hardware. No sim-to-real gap. Now the flywheel is running: their fleet collects scenes in production, every scene rolls out in our world model, new failures and slow behavior surface in sim, and an improved RL model ships on top of their unchanged policy. Each turn of the loop, the robots get faster and more reliable. No need to spend weeks wrangling with robot operators and hardware inconsistencies or waiting months for a new foundation model. Schedule a meeting if you have robots in production and want them to work faster and more reliably week over week: https://lnkd.in/eY8yrim2

For years my wallpaper has been this quote now… I just tried to laser in & had unwavering belief in God & myself (to figure things out) I learned fast, then learned to execute fast (still working on it) So to anyone reading… take every intro, work really hard, take risks Decide what’s important to you (even if that means shutting down) reminder: life ends when you die You can enter the arena at any age, you can outgrow your peers and you can out execute the former you 😊 — P.S This is a rushed post out together of things that seemed to resonate with interesting friends on X , so decided to share here too :)
